target_customer: Ambulance operators and EMS agencies, priced at 2,000 dollars per month per the demo day post
problem: Ambulance crews spend about 40 minutes of a two-hour run on paperwork.
business_model: B2B SaaS, 2,000 dollars per month (demo day post, Sept 2016)

founders.name: Nupur Mehta
founders.background_notes: YC page and Founder Institute post. Interned at Stanford Hospital and the Goodman Simulation Center.

founders.name: Tejaswi Sagiraju
founders.background_notes: Named as developer and co-founder on the Founder Institute demo day post; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Forms with pre-fill, barcodes and onboard Wi-Fi devices, but integration with hospital and state EMS data systems added work.

defensibility.rationale: Established ePCR vendors such as ImageTrend, ESO and Zoll had agency relationships and state approvals; a small startup had little protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: These vendors stayed dominant and consolidated; no acquisition of RigPlenish found.

market_need_then: Demo day post claims paperwork time falls from 40 to 4 minutes, a 1.3 billion dollar market and a pilot covering 4.4 million runs; all company claims.

brand_strength.rationale: Awkward coined name and no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: RigPlenish aimed to automate ambulance run paperwork at 2,000 dollars a month and presented at YC Summer 2016 demo day. No funding, customers beyond a claimed pilot, or shutdown news was found, so the cause of inactivity is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: Website rigplenish.com did not resolve (host not found), treated as dead or blocked. Competitor list left empty because search found only undated vendor directories; named ePCR incumbents are in takeover_risk without dated sources. Crunchbase says founded 2015. Name origin not found.
